C0.quote: the legislators voting for or against the proposal
C0.note: Borderline. The main object is informational lobbying, but the model includes a legislative vote under an M-majority requirement, and results are tied to that requirement. Coded ELIG.

C1.quote: The solution concept is (pure-strategy) Perfect Bayesian equilibrium
C1.note: Equilibrium stopping rule and search sequence are the main results. Section 6.1 compares legislators' expected payoffs with and without lobbying (welfare).

C2.1.value: vote (voting strategy: vote for or against the proposal)
C2.1.quote: the legislators voting for or against the proposal

C2.2.quote: the legislators voting for or against the proposal
C2.2.note: Binary vote in favor of or against a single allocation proposal.

C2.3.quote: Each district has a valuation of the goods
C2.3.note: Districts have valuations and legislators have payoffs u_n(g).

C2.4.quote: votes in favor of the proposal if she is better off
C2.4.note: Votes (voting strategy) and valuations/payoffs are separate objects with separate notation.

C3.1.quote: votes in favor of the proposal if she is better off
C3.1.note: Legislators vote for the proposal iff it improves their payoff. No analysis considers voting against the held attitude. The strategic agents are IG and AS.

C3.2.quote: votes in favor of the proposal if she is better off
C3.2.note: Statement in words that the vote follows the legislator's payoff. Weak statement.

C3.3.quote: weakly undominated voting strategies for the legislators
C3.3.note: The vote follows from the equilibrium solution concept with the weakly-undominated refinement. No separate sincerity argument is given.

C4.1.note: Input format is a binary vote (OTH), not RANK/WEAK/APPR/DICH/PAIR.

C5.1.note: Compares expected payoffs of all players with and without lobbying and examines who gains and loses; Example 5 shows all legislators except AS worse off.

C5.2.note: Welfare is evaluated on legislators' payoffs u_n(g), defined separately from votes.

VOT.quote_behav: votes in favor of the proposal if she is better off
VOT.note: Legislators best-respond using the prior and the publicly observed signals.

CAN.note: Districts are only recipients of goods.

ORG.quote_behav: AS proposes an allocation g that maximizes his expected utility
ORG.quote_info: Realized valuations are unknown to IG and the legislators.
ORG.note: Agenda setter (chair) chooses the allocation proposal. Knows the prior and the public signals.

BRI.note: IG is coded under OTH, not as a briber (it provides verifiable information, no payments).

DES.note: The majority requirement M is a parameter, not a designer's choice.

OTH.quote_behav: The interest group engages in selective persuasion
OTH.quote_info: Realized valuations are unknown to IG and the legislators.
OTH.note: Interest group (lobbyist) chooses a sequential search of districts. Knows the priors p_n and observes signals, but not the realized valuations.

C7.1.note: All present types (voters, agenda setter, interest group) are modelled as strategic.

C8.1.quote: The solution concept is (pure-strategy) Perfect Bayesian equilibrium
C8.1.note: PBE solved by backward induction over the stages.
